_README: MARKER-ONLY. English only. Fetched lazily by the engine when a teacher/marker PDF is built. Never rendered on the student-facing page.

markingScheme.criterion: Quotes at least two of their own Photon Lab measurements taken at the same sunlight but different cell temperatures, giving the electrical power in watts for each.
markingScheme.accept: Any two genuine rows from the Investigation Record (Lab = PV cell) with the same sunlight value and different temperatures, e.g. 'at 1000 W and 0 °C I got 242 W, at 1000 W and 65 °C I got 185 W'. Check the figures against the Record table. Rows labelled 'Panel A' / 'Panel B' count.
markingScheme.insufficient: A general statement with no figures; figures from only one test; or two tests that differ in sunlight instead of temperature.

markingScheme.criterion: Describes the trend: with the sunlight unchanged, the electrical power (or efficiency) of the panel decreased as the cell temperature increased.
markingScheme.accept: 'The hotter the cell, the less electricity' / 'efficiency fell as it warmed' / 'the cold panel produced more'. A reason (silicon is less efficient when hot; panels need light, not heat) is welcome but not required for this mark.
markingScheme.insufficient: States that hotter panels produce more power, or describes only the effect of changing the sunlight.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains the fate of the unconverted solar power: it is not destroyed but transferred to other forms, mostly thermal energy (heat) in the panel, with some light reflected (conservation of energy / First Law of Thermodynamics).
markingScheme.accept: 'It became heat (and some was reflected)'; 'energy cannot be destroyed, so the rest turned into heat'. Naming the First Law is not required if the transfer to heat is stated. Credit use of their own heat/reflected figures.
markingScheme.insufficient: 'It was lost' or 'wasted' with no statement of what it became; or 'it was destroyed / disappeared'.

markingScheme.criterion: A feature that captures and/or stores the Sun's energy, with how it works: EITHER large Sun-facing windows that let solar radiation in to warm the interior, OR thermal mass (concrete floor, brick or stone walls) that absorbs and stores thermal energy by day and releases it gradually after sunset.
markingScheme.accept: 'Big windows facing the Sun (north in the Southern Hemisphere / south in the Northern Hemisphere) let sunlight in to heat the floor'; 'a concrete floor soaks up heat in the day and gives it out at night'. Either windows or thermal mass earns the mark if its function is explained.
markingScheme.insufficient: Names a feature with no explanation of how it works; or recommends solar panels / a heater (not passive).

markingScheme.criterion: A feature that reduces heat loss, with how it works: insulation in walls/roof OR double glazing, reducing the transfer of thermal energy from the warm interior to the colder outside.
markingScheme.accept: 'Insulation slows heat escaping through the walls and roof'; 'double glazing traps a layer of air/gas so less heat passes through the window'.
markingScheme.insufficient: 'Insulation keeps the cold out' with no reference to heat transfer/escape; or a feature named with no function.

markingScheme.criterion: A feature that prevents summer overheating, with how it works: a roof overhang (eaves/shading) that blocks the high-angle summer Sun from shining directly through the glass, while the low winter Sun can still pass underneath.
markingScheme.accept: 'A roof overhang shades the window in summer when the Sun is high'. The winter half of the explanation is not required. Also accept external shading/blinds or deciduous trees with the same reasoning about blocking direct summer sunlight.
markingScheme.insufficient: 'Air conditioning' or 'a fan' (not passive); or 'an overhang' with no explanation of what it blocks.

criteria.source: Auto-marked from the Knowledge Check (auto_marked_score). The teacher does not mark this row.
= the Explain question's 3-point marking scheme above, one-to-one. Do not award these marks a second time here.

levels.descriptor: None of the three Explain points achieved: no own measurements quoted, the temperature trend not described, and the fate of the unconverted power not explained.

Any ONE of the three Explain points achieved: (a) quotes two of their own measurements at the same sunlight and different cell temperatures with the electrical power, (b) describes that electrical power fell as the cell got hotter, or (c) explains that the unconverted power was transferred mostly as heat, with some reflected, not destroyed.
Any TWO of those three Explain points achieved.

All THREE achieved: two own measurements quoted (same sunlight, different temperatures, watts given), the trend described (hotter cell, less electrical power), and the unconverted power explained as transferred to heat and reflected light, not destroyed.

criteria.source: = the Apply question's 3-point marking scheme above, one-to-one. Do not award these marks a second time here.

levels.descriptor: None of the three Apply points achieved.

Any ONE of the three Apply points achieved: (a) a capture/storage feature (Sun-facing windows or thermal mass) with how it works, (b) a heat-loss feature (insulation or double glazing) with how it works, or (c) a summer feature (roof overhang or equivalent shading) with how it works.
Any TWO of those three Apply points achieved.
All THREE achieved: a capture/storage feature, a heat-loss feature and a summer-overheating feature, each with a correct explanation of how it works.

criteria.source: Assessed holistically across the Explain and Apply answers together. Independent of, and never overlapping with, the content marks above.

levels.descriptor: Too unclear or incomplete for the reasoning to be followed reliably.
Main meaning understandable, but organisation, precision or scientific vocabulary has problems (e.g. 'the sun power got used up', features listed without sentences).

Clear and logical, in full sentences, using appropriate terms correctly (e.g. efficiency, thermal energy, reflected, thermal mass, insulation, radiation). Minor spelling or grammar slips that do not affect meaning are not penalised.

markingInstructions: Mark ONLY the two constructed responses (Explain and Apply). Use each question's point-by-point marking scheme and award each point independently. The rubric rows 'Evidence and explanation' and 'Applying the science' restate those same points as 0-3 bands and equal the Explain and Apply marks one-to-one (see each row's source); never add them a second time. Communication (0-2) is the only holistic mark and is judged across both answers together. Copy the auto-marked Knowledge Check score into 'Knowledge & understanding' (max 8). Total = 8 + 3 + 3 + 2 = 16. Verify any figures the student quotes against the Investigation Record table: rows with Lab = 'PV cell' show sunlight and cell temperature in Setup and the electricity, heat and reflected light in Result. In this model a 1 m2 panel is 22 % efficient at 25 °C and loses 0.4 % of its output per degree above that, so at 1000 W it gives about 242 W at 0 °C, 220 W at 25 °C and 185 W at 65 °C. Accept scientifically valid alternative wording per each point's 'accept' field; do not penalise spelling unless meaning is unclear. Report: total, percentage, score by criterion, one strength, one correction, one next step, in under 80 words.
